chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had Dinars owed to him by another man, so he assigned another man in place of the debtor for the Dinars. Can he take them as Dirhams at the current exchange rate? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he desires.'

key_terms.أَحَالَ: To assign or delegate a debt to another party
key_terms.سِعْرِ الْيَوْمِ: The exchange rate of the day

ai.seo_question: Can a creditor convert a gold debt into silver currency at the current exchange rate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of 'hiyalah' (debt assignment) as a valid mechanism for currency exchange, allowing a creditor to settle a gold dinar debt with silver dirhams at the current market rate. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that such transactions are permissible provided the exchange is immediate and avoids the elements of riba (usury) associated with delayed or unequal exchanges of the same currency type.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had some Dinars for him upon a man, so he assigned another man with the Dinars. Can he take it as Dirham with the (exchange) rate on the day?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, if he so desires it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man to whom another man owed a certain amount of dinars and he assigned another man to collect it from him; if he could take it in the form of dirhams for the current rate. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, if he wanted . 555
